cards.front: In an if / else-if chain, in which order are conditions checked?
cards.back: Top-down; the first condition that is true runs its block and the rest are skipped
cards.extra: The article calls this the defining behaviour of else-if: checking stops at the first true outcome, so specific cases must come before general ones.
cards.source: educative.io — What are conditional statements in programming?

cards.front: What role does the else block play in a conditional chain?
cards.back: It is the default — it runs only when every earlier condition returned false
cards.extra: It cannot have its own condition. Omit it and a non-matching value simply does nothing, which is sometimes the bug.
cards.source: educative.io — What are conditional statements in programming?

cards.front: Why use switch instead of an if/else-if chain?
cards.back: It expresses one value, many branches more clearly than a repeated comparison
cards.extra: Each case ends with break; the default covers the no-match path. Readability is the whole argument — the semantics are equivalent.
cards.source: educative.io — What are conditional statements in programming?

cards.front: What happens if no switch case matches and there is no default?
cards.back: Nothing runs — the switch simply falls through to the next statement after it
cards.extra: That silence hides bugs that a default branch with a thrown exception would surface immediately.
cards.source: educative.io — What are conditional statements in programming?
